plan.title: Sensor resilience plan
plan.summary: The current sensor classes show a working demo but not a durable client. The main issue is that a socket failure or server shutdown kills the sensor thread. The next fix should focus on connection lifecycle, automatic retry, clean shutdown, and clearer protocol handling.

what_is_good.item: Each sensor is a separate runnable task, which is a good base for independent data generation.
The code is easy to read and the sensor types are easy to understand.
Using try-with-resources is a good direction for stream cleanup.
The sensor logic is simple enough to reason about for a small prototype.

what_needs_fixing.item: The sensor should not exit permanently when the server is unavailable; it should reconnect.
Socket reads should not rely on BufferedReader.ready(). It is not a reliable network signal.
There is no explicit shutdown path for threads.
Hardcoded host, port, delay, and ranges make the code harder to maintain and test.
Existing error handling prints a generic message but does not recover or retry.

step.name: Build a reconnect loop
step.description: Instead of creating one socket and exiting on failure, the sensor should keep a running loop: connect, send data, handle failure, wait, reconnect.

step.name: Introduce a stop flag
step.description: Use an interruptable or volatile boolean to allow the thread to stop cleanly when the application ends.

step.name: Add retry/backoff
step.description: After a failed connection or timeout, wait a short time before retrying and increase the delay if the server stays down.

step.name: Separate value generation from networking
step.description: One component should generate the reading; another should manage the socket and retry policy.

step.name: Define a clear message contract
step.description: Decide on a stable payload format, such as name + value + delimiter, and make sure the server and client both understand it.

example_design.description: Conceptual example only. This is not the project code; it is a model for the intended approach.

example_stop_pattern.description: Conceptual example of a shutdown pattern that avoids leaving threads stuck.

risk_summary.item: Without reconnect logic, a server crash permanently kills the sensor client.
Without stop handling, shutdown becomes unreliable.
Without a proper protocol, it becomes difficult to distinguish valid data from malformed messages.
Without clear retry handling, the system can spin aggressively during downtime.

plan.final_recommendation: The next step is to turn the sensor into a self-healing client with reconnect + retry + clean shutdown logic. That solves the most important issue before any feature work or protocol cleanup is added.
